prompt: Decide whether two meetings overlap (meetings that merely touch at an endpoint do not) and measure a meeting's length in minutes with Duration. Complete overlaps and minutesBetween in MeetingPlanner.
explanation: Two half-open ranges overlap exactly when each one starts before the other one ends: aStart.isBefore(bEnd) && bStart.isBefore(aEnd). Because isBefore is strict (9:00 is not before 9:00), meetings that merely touch at an endpoint fail one of the two comparisons automatically -- no special case needed. Duration.between measures the gap between two temporal objects, and toMinutes() converts the whole Duration to a count of minutes.
hints: Think about when two ranges DO NOT overlap: one of them ends at or before the other starts.
aStart.isBefore(bEnd) && bStart.isBefore(aEnd) -- strict isBefore makes touching endpoints count as no overlap.
java.time.Duration.between(start, end) returns a Duration; call .toMinutes() on it.
